Boisterous

BOY-stur-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Boisterous is noisy, energetic, and cheerful; rowdy in a good-natured way.

The boisterous family reunion filled the backyard with shouting cousins, cannonballing kids, and a very loud game of horseshoes.

Worked Example

By the third quarter, the boisterous home crowd was chanting, stomping, and waving banners so loudly that players couldn't hear the referee's whistle.

Boisterous loudness comes from excitement and good cheer -- it's rowdy, but in a fun, high-spirited way rather than an angry or harsh one.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rowdy: noisy and disorderly, in a lively way

spirited: full of energy and enthusiasm

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

subdued: quiet and restrained

tranquil: calm and peaceful

Where it sits · how loud and wild the energy gets — lively → boisterous → unruly

lively vs. boisterous: Lively means energetic, without necessarily being especially loud the way boisterous is.

unruly vs. boisterous: Unruly pushes boisterous's rowdy energy even further, into wilder, harder-to-control behavior.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — boistous

root — boistous: rough, coarse, unrefined (Middle English, ultimate origin debated -- possibly from Old French boisteus)

Put it together

Put it together: Boisterous comes from the Middle English word boistous, meaning rough or coarse; most etymologists trace it no further back with real confidence, since its ultimate origin before that is still debated.

Use the root in a new word: boisterously

Use the root in a new word: boisterously: The team celebrated boisterously, dumping an entire cooler of ice water over their coach's head.
